evaluation.scoring: harness: required_tools, answer_contains, answer_contains_any, numeric_check, expect_tool_error
evaluation.tools_protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — calculator, word_count, web_search, get_weather

v2_lora.notes: v2 evaluation used the corrected two-pass tool-call parser (see serving/colab_server_v2.py). The single tool error in eval_results_v2.json (calculator returning division-by-zero for adversarial_division_by_zero) is the EXPECTED behavior that task requires — the task scored PASS.

e4_lora_fixed_parser.notes: E4 controlled ablation: V1 adapter (35 trajectories) evaluated with V2 two-pass parser. Intended to isolate the parser effect; reported score came from a notebook-local evaluation loop with a different tool stack (see docs/e4-experiment-guide.md, added 2026-10-09). Tavily = real. Per-task traces not captured; only pass/fail recorded.

v1_vs_e4.description: Same V1 adapter; parser changed, and (as run) evaluation client/tool stack and date also changed
v1_vs_e4.note: Parser produced zero net aggregate change. Two tasks recovered, two newly failed — net 0.

e4_vs_v2.description: Data effect: same V2 parser, augmented training data
e4_vs_v2.note: All 5 E4 failures recovered by V2's 11 additional targeted trajectories. Data effect = full +5 aggregate improvement.

methodology_notes.controlled_comparison: All four evaluations (Base, V1, E4, V2) used the same 23 tasks, same max_steps=3, same MCP tool infrastructure, same base model, and greedy decoding (do_sample=False).
methodology_notes.scoring_immutability: Benchmark tasks in eval/tasks.py were not modified between the three evaluations. The scoring harness was not modified.
methodology_notes.parser_change: v1 evaluation used a single-pass regex parser in the Colab server. v2 and E4 evaluations used a corrected two-pass parser (serving/colab_server_v2.py / colab_server_e4.py). The parser was identified as a contributing factor in v1 failures where the fine-tuned model emitted malformed tool-call tags.
methodology_notes.training_data_change: v2 added 11 targeted trajectories to address specific failure patterns identified by trace-level analysis of v1 (word_count→calculator, weather→calculator, 3-tool chains, division-by-zero error handling, false-premise rejection).
methodology_notes.confound_resolution: [Corrected 2026-10-09] E4 (V1 adapter + V2 parser) = 18/23, the same aggregate as V1, with 4 task flips. E4 was scored with a notebook-local evaluation loop and tool stack that differ from the Base/V1/V2 client, so it does not give a parser-only estimate. The +5 from E4 to V2 coincides with a retraining run that changed the data (35 to 46, failure-informed) and the optimizer/memory settings together. Earlier text read: 'resolved by E4 ... parser effect = 0 ... +5 attributable to the augmented training data'.

scope_limitations: Pass rates are tied to this specific 23-task set (fixed, but not held out from V2 development).
Generalization beyond this benchmark is not implied.
All four evaluations used max_steps=3; larger step budgets might give different results.

V2's 11 added trajectories were written after inspecting V1 failures on this benchmark; prompts are disjoint from the 23 evaluation prompts but several follow the same task templates (evaluation-adaptation risk).
[Superseded 2026-09-16] An earlier note here said running V1's adapter under V2's parser would not be a fair comparison; that run is E4, the controlled parser ablation.

base_model.notes: All three evaluations used the same base model with no adapter.

training_config.verified: Exact QLoRA hyperparameters from training scripts and adapter_config.json

config.optimizer: V1: Trainer default (not set in colab_train_7b.py); V2: bnb PagedAdamW8bit with gradient checkpointing and use_cache=False (colab_train_7b_v2.py). Corrected 2026-10; see provenance/hyperparameters.md.

base.notes: Untuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct evaluated with colab_server.py (single-pass parser)

v1_lora.notes: LoRA v1 adapter trained on 35 trajectories (training_data.jsonl) with colab_server.py (single-pass parser)

v2_lora.notes: LoRA v2 adapter trained on 46 trajectories (training_data_augmented.jsonl) with colab_server_v2.py (two-pass parser)

e4_lora_fixed_parser.notes: E4 controlled ablation: V1 LoRA adapter (35 trajectories) with V2 two-pass parser. Tavily real API. Intended to isolate parser from data effect; evaluation client also differed (see docs/e4-experiment-guide.md).

confound_note.statement: E4 (V1 adapter + V2 parser = 18/23) holds the V1 adapter fixed; aggregate change E4 − V1 = 0 tasks, but E4 also changed the evaluation client/tool stack, so this is not a parser-only estimate (correction 2026-10-09). Remaining difference V2 − E4 = +5 tasks, which changes the adapter, the training data (35 → 46) and the V2 run's optimizer/gradient-checkpointing settings together.
confound_note.resolution: E4 completed 2026-09-16: aggregate unchanged under parser + evaluation-client change; no parser-only estimate exists. Full +5 improvement coincides with the V2 retraining run (targeted augmentation plus memory-related optimizer settings); it is not an isolated data effect.

environment.notes: Training was run on Google Colab T4 GPU (CUDA 12.x, driver version not recorded). Inference servers also on Colab T4. Local eval client runs on CPU-only venv.

random_seeds.notes: No random seeds were set in training scripts or evaluation scripts. The eval uses greedy decoding (do_sample=False) which is deterministic given the same model output. However, model generation without explicit seed may have non-determinism from CUDA operations.
